title: Directional Priors for Volumetric Root Segmentation
abstract: Plant root systems exhibit strong directional growth patterns that can be non-destructively measured by X-ray CT imaging, but the scale of the resulting high-resolution volumes makes segmentation challenging. We propose representing these directional priors as dense vector fields encoding local root growth direction, and incorporate them into a cascaded 3D U-Net architecture. The first stage jointly predicts a binary segmentation mask and a dense vector field; the second stage then refines this segmentation by conditioning on the predicted field, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on our new benchmark dataset. Incorporating the predicted vector fields to guide patch traversal at inference also increases efficiency, maintaining 99.63\% ground-truth coverage while visiting only 13.44\% of the volume, promoting accurate and efficient root phenotyping at scale. All code and our new dataset are publicly available.
